summary: 40-foot wooden DNR live-in tower built 1956 on Weatherwax Ridge, Grays Harbor County; staffed in the early 1960s and removed in 1968. No lookout tower stands today.

facts.design: 40-foot wooden DNR live-in tower with 14 by 14 foot cab
facts.status_note: Removed in 1968 (FireLookout.com says destroyed). Communication towers stand at one point on the ridge; the old lookout stood at another, on a lower knob.

access.note: A gate on the 200 road is meant to keep people off the highest ridge; the sources do not say whether walkers may pass it. Ask the land manager before going past it.

visit.trail_note: Willhite's route runs up the 200 road past that gate: 1.3 miles with 600 feet of gain. The old road over the lower knob can still be followed, per his visit.

notes_for_editor: Sources agree on the 1956 build and the 1968 removal, except FireLookout.com's 'Destroyed 1968' (story notes the difference). Elevation differs: the register gives 2,710 ft (826 m, which the record uses) while Willhite's header gives 2,680 feet; not resolved and not used in the story. The 1960-1964 keepers come only from Willhite. The tree lookout year is 'mid-1940s' and is not given as an event. Access is marked restricted because of the gate; no source says whether walkers may pass it, and the story does not encourage passing it. Ownership is listed as DNR by the register, while Willhite describes the south side of the ridge as private land and the north as Olympic National Forest; the lookout's own parcel is not confirmed.
